That necessity is unproved: the target keys are fixed and only final freshness is mandatory. O5 stipulates one refresh-associated wrong-target write through retained row selection. The causal_return_path_hypothesis that this mismatch requests another refresh, reorders a subsequent selection and repeats the error is an unobserved feedback hypothesis. Examine both refresh -> changed row identity -> mismatch and the reversed arrow mismatch -> refresh; neither repeated feedback nor a successful correction trace is supplied.

predictions.account: Rival hypothesis: mismatch-triggered refresh drives recurrence through the return link, beyond the initial reorder.
predictions.when: In separate scripted replays, hold the initial target demand K2/K5/K7, valued outcome, initial state and scheduled ordinary refreshes fixed. predictions.result: The feedback hypothesis predicts that suppressing the return link removes extra mismatch-triggered refreshes and any later wrong-key writes attributable to their reordering, while the stipulated initial miswrite remains in its diagnostic arm. Recurrence should depend on a return refresh actually changing a retained selection; an extra refresh alone is insufficient. Comparable recurrence without the return link would weaken this account. Diagnostic arms may fail the unchanged no-wrong-write outcome; no successful future is asserted.

predictions.account: Rival reversed-arrow hypothesis: mismatches cause refresh requests, while scheduled snapshot changes independently cause row-binding errors.
predictions.when: At matched scripted request gates, independently withhold or inject an intended/actual mismatch notification, holding the existing commit log, ordinary refresh schedule and selection binding fixed; retain the final latest-snapshot refresh. If changing order with row binding still causes errors when notifications are suppressed, mismatch -> refresh and refresh -> mismatch are distinct causal arrows. Their presence does not establish a self-repeating loop; all notification interventions and recurrence claims remain model hypotheses.
